subject: Request: temporary p95 relief during migration + measurement handoff
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@argonhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Granger <tom.granger@argonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term p95 relief ask during DB migration

Hi Markus,

Quick note from our ops team — we have a scheduled database migration and cache refresh window next week (Jul 13-14) that will temporarily increase end-to-end response tails. Our SREs estimate the hosted inference p95 could slip to ~1.8s for a 3–6 hour window during the cutover.

We wanted to request a temporary, documented carveout (p95 padding) for that maintenance window so our on-call doesn't automatically trigger a contractual SLA escalation. We understand this is an exception; we can provide telemetry and a post-mortem.

Can Redwood confirm if a time-boxed exception is possible, and what evidence you need (token-level traces, KV cache hit rates, request IDs)?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Site Reliability
Argon Health

(Attachment: Argon_SLO_Migration_Timeline.pdf)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@argonhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term p95 relief ask during DB migration

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We can accommodate a short, documented exception, but need a clear mutual action plan. High level we need:

- Exact maintenance window (start/end with timezone)
- Expected traffic delta and sample request IDs during the window
- Post-migration telemetry: sample traces, token-level latency histograms, and KV cache warmup curve
- Confirmation that Argon will not change routing or traffic shape outside the stated window

Operationally we'll:
- Create a temporary p95 padding rule for the specified window (we'll call it a transient-tail relief)
- Enable additional logging and request-id retention for 72 hours after the window
- Collect Redwood-side evidence (Scheduler logs, model queue depths, cold-KV-rate) to attach to the amendment

Attachment-wise, please also export a KV warm-start profile (kvcache-warmup-profile.csv) so we can correlate cache misses to tail spikes.

Ben/lauren — looping you for approval and notes on how we'll formalize this in the contract (short addendum vs operational carveout).

I can draft the amendment today if you confirm the window.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

(Inline: quoted Argon timeline attached)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: suggested carveout language + rollback guardrails

Markus / Lauren — quick internal note before we send the formal addendum:

Suggested carveout language (short):
"Redwood will apply a time-bound operational adjustment to p95 latency commitments for Argon Health for the maintenance window Jul 13 22:00 UTC - Jul 14 04:00 UTC. This adjustment is limited to the stated window and contingent on Argon providing pre- and post-migration telemetry. Redwood will not issue credits for metrics falling within the approved window."

Rollback / guardrails:
- If degradation extends beyond 6 hours, the carveout auto-expires and normal SLO rules reapply and the incident will be evaluated for credits per the base SLA.
- Redwood will provide a consolidated evidence pack within 5 business days (SLO-evidence-pack.zip) including request traces and queue metrics.

Also recommend we require the KV warmup CSV and sample request IDs at least 48 hours prior to the window — helps our ops team pre-stage extra logging.

If OK, I can post the addendum into DocuSign and copy legal for a quick sign-off.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@argonhealth.com>, Tom Granger <tom.granger@argonhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term p95 relief ask during DB migration — plan & next steps

Elena / Tom —

Thanks — we reviewed and can proceed with the plan below. Please confirm you can provide the KV warm-start CSV and 100 sample request IDs by Jul 11 16:00 PDT. Once we have those we will:

1) Prepare a short addendum (time-boxed carveout clause) and route to DocuSign.
2) Enable the transient-tail relief rule in production for Jul 13 22:00 UTC - Jul 14 04:00 UTC.
3) Retain request-level traces and our queue/cold-KV metrics for 72 hours post-window.
4) Deliver a joint evidence pack within 5 business days and a short post-mortem within 7 business days.

If Argon anticipates the window shifting more than 60 minutes, call out the change ASAP — we'll coordinate but note that any shift >60m requires re-signing the addendum.

I'll attach the addendum draft and a short checklist to this thread after you confirm the artifacts timeline.

Best,
Markus

(Attachments: SLO-evidence-pack.zip — template, DocuSign link to follow)
